title: Photoshop Post-Processing of a Coastal Landscape: Layered Compositing, Light Separation, and Sky Drama

date.basis: embedded_creation_time metadata; export/creation timestamp; transcript does not confirm shooting date

locations.name: coastal shoreline with sea stacks (inferred)
locations.basis: Transcript repeatedly identifies a coastal scene with waves, cliffs and rocks; no explicit shooting location is named

summary: This video presents a Photoshop-based landscape post-production workflow focused on turning a telephoto coastal capture into a three-layer composite with a dramatic sky. The instructor guides image selection from multiple shore frames, uses cloning and healing brushes to place rocks, waves, and birds, then builds a three-zone workflow (light on rocks, layer separation, sky drama) using whites, selective color, mid-tone dodge, de-haze, and color grading. The session emphasizes non-destructive editing, saving multiple versions, and achieving directional light with careful edge handling and beam effects to enhance atmosphere.

Whites adjustment and tonal tweaks for dynamic range

opacity-based blending and layer painting for rock illumination
mid-tone dodge to introduce directional light
shadow dodge/burn to recover shadow detail
de-haze and tonal color grading for sky and background
drama in the sky and multi-pass highlight regrades

non-destructive workflow with multiple saved versions

sections.title: Shot scouting and primary selection
sections.description: Identify usable frames from the coastal sequence, open preferred images, and set aside the rest. This section centers on choosing the main cliff/wave shot with strong layered composition to anchor the final composite.

sections.title: Initial comp and element placement
concepts: prepping for layering the primary shot
sections.description: Open and apply prior adjustments to additional frames, begin positioning elements (rocks, cliffs) with cloning-paint work to start forming the composite structure.

sections.title: Bird repositioning and prep for integration
sections.description: Identify a suitable bird shot, then use the healing brush to relocate or clean up small elements while preserving edges for a natural blend.

sections.title: Water texture remix and layering prep
sections.description: Blend water textures from multiple frames, align waves with existing layers, and prepare the scene for the three-layer separation that follows.

sections.title: Three-layer separation concept (rocks, layers, sky)
sections.description: Outline the three-zone approach: emphasize light on rock faces, ensure natural separation between layers with telephoto advantages, and prepare for dramatic sky work.

sections.title: Dramatic sky and tonal color grading (initial)
concepts: reducing saturation in favor of blue on neutral grays
sections.description: Apply tonal adjustments to establish mood, introduce blue on neutral grays, and start broader highlight shaping to enhance the sky drama.

sections.title: Non-destructive workflow and versioning
sections.description: Demonstrate saving separate versions of the artwork to compare dramatic vs. natural looks and preserve the original pixels for non-destructive edits.

sections.title: Beams and atmospheric effects
sections.description: Explore adding atmospheric beams through careful brushwork, de-hazing, and selective saturation adjustments. The segment covers creating clean, feathered lines and balancing sky-ground contrast for a convincing atmospheric effect.
